Author: Pankaj Bhatia
Bench: Pankaj Bhatia
High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
?Neutral Citation No. - 2023:Ahc:165241
Court No. - 66
Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 31679 of 2021
Applicant :- Jishan

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Opposite Party :- State of U.P.
Counsel for Applicant :- Sujata Choudhary,Mohit Kumar Singh
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Pankaj Bhatia,J.
1.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant, learned AGA and perused the record.
2. The FIR in question was lodged alleging that the daughter of the informant was married with the applicant who used to demand dowry and used to harass her.
It is alleged that on 10.12.2020 when the demand of dowry was not fulfilled, the entire family had killed the daughter of the informant.
In the FIR, the entire family has been roped in.

3. Contention of learned counsel for the applicant is that as per the post-mortem report, the cause of death could not be ascertained and the viscera was sent for further examination, as such, there is no conclusive reason for the cause of death.

He argues that apart from the statement of the victim,
prima-facie, no material exists to demonstrate that immediately or in the near past, the victim was Jishan vs State Of U.P. on 17 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/168096439/
1 harassed in relation to demand of dowry or the same was the cause of death.
He argues that the post-mortem report on record does not indicate any visible injury over the body in question.
He further argues that the applicant is husband and is in custody since 23.12.2020 and has no criminal antecedent.
4. Learned AGA has opposed the bail application.

5. Considering the submissions made at the Bar, prima-facie, the averments in the FIR indicated the cause of death as non-payment of dowry, however, apart from the said statement, there is no material in the form of statement or otherwise to satisfy the requirement of Section 304B IPC to the effect that soon before her death, the victim was subjected to cruelty or harassment by the husband or any relative in connection with any demand of dowry.
The applicant is in custody since more than three years and has no criminal antecedent.

Thus, taking into consideration the length of incarceration and prima-facie, there being no material as recorded above coupled with the fact that the applicant has no criminal antecedent and there is nothing on record to demonstrate that the applicant, if enlarged on bail, can in any way adversely affect the trial, the applicant is entitled to be enlarged on bail.
In view thereof, the application is allowed.

6. Let the applicant Jishan be released on bail in FIR No.583 of 2020, under Section 304B, 498A IPC & Section 3/4 of Dowry Prohibition Act, P.S. Kithore, District Meerut on his furnishing a personal bond with two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of court concerned with the following conditions:
(a) The applicant shall execute a bond to undertake to attend the hearings;
(b) The applicant shall not commit any offence similar to the offence of which he is accused or suspected of the commission; and (c) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
